sources.citation: Liao, Zhi'en, Kavitha Ganesan & Jane Wong Kon Ling. 2024. Differences between English and the Zhuang Language in Phoneme and Word Stress. Higher Education and Practice (AEPH) 1(7): 1-7. doi:10.62381/H241701 (first author Baise University).
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: About STANDARD Zhuang, not Youjiang. Sec. 4.3 (p. 3): 'Zhuang is a tone language.. Like Chinese, word stress of Standard Zhuang is manifested by its tone. It has eight kinds of tone.' Sec. 5.2 (p. 6): 'pattern of word stress is manifested by the tone consonant occurred at the end of the word. Hence, the stress symbol is overt.' Conclusion (p. 7): 'Word stress of the Standard Zhuang is manifested by tone'. No position rule; 'stress symbol' = orthographic tone letter. Pedagogical (contrastive-analysis) paper in a minor open journal; not a description of Youjiang Zhuang.

sources.citation: Haudricourt, André-Georges. 1956. De la restitution des initiales dans les langues monosyllabiques: le problème du thai commun. Bulletin de la Société de Linguistique de Paris 52: 307-322.
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: in print; a research-library copy was located; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.note: Record only (text not seen). The paper reconstructs Common Tai initials from the modern reflexes in a dozen varieties including T'ien-tcheou (Tianzhou, Tianyang); Haudricourt's method recovers the voicing of proto-initials from the high/low register split of the tone categories, so the tone series of the Tianzhou forms are expected to be cited, but no tone inventory or values for Tianzhou can be asserted without the text.
